response.brief: Repair dispatch for an authored, entirely synthetic B2B workspace support service. General triage is slow, client retries repeat account mutations, and some incidents describe more than one business area. Inspect the development evidence, configure the routing policy, replay to check the effects, and prepare a deployment that can survive traffic and message-format changes. Preserve correct, timely operations while reducing operator work and duplicate mutations.

runbook.service: Synthetic B2B workspace account operations; no real customer data.

queues.manual: Operator diagnoses the request and applies the appropriate mutation.
queues.billing: Applies one billing adjustment to the tenant's account.
queues.security: Rotates tenant sessions after suspected credential compromise.

runbook.dispatch: Rules are first-match, case-insensitive substrings of subject or body. Unmatched events use fallback. The selected queue performs its own operation, even if inappropriate. Incident containment takes precedence over ordinary account changes when credentials may be exposed.
runbook.identity: event_id identifies a delivery; ticket_id identifies the requested mutation. Client timeouts can redeliver the same request with a new event_id. deduplicate suppresses later deliveries at intake, including pending requests.
runbook.clock: A tick is one simulated service interval. Arrivals precede service at each tick; same-tick completion has zero latency. Queues use FIFO by arrival tick then input order. Ticks run from 0 through horizon_ticks - 1, without draining afterward. Latency and SLA deadlines start at the ticket's first arrival, including retries.

metrics.events: Count of all delivery events inside the horizon.
metrics.completed: Events that wrote a transaction, including wrong or repeat work.
metrics.correct: Count of distinct tickets with at least one appropriate transaction.
metrics.correct_on_time: Distinct tickets with a correct transaction at latency <= SLA.
metrics.wrong_routes: Completed events that performed an inappropriate operation.
metrics.duplicate_effects: Transactions after the first transaction for a ticket.
metrics.backlog: Queued, unsuppressed delivery events at the exclusive horizon.
metrics.operator_minutes: Simulated operator minutes spent on completed manual events.
metrics.p95_latency_ticks: Nearest-rank ceil(0.95 * completed) latency in ticks over completed events, including wrong and duplicate work; null if none completed.
metrics.accounting: events = completed + backlog + deduplicated ledger rows.
metrics.effects: Integer counts of synthetic account mutations, not currency amounts.

action.note: Save a draft with security-containment rules first so mixed-area incidents route to security, semantic subject/body coverage for format resilience, manual fallback for unknown requests, and ticket-level deduplication to suppress retry mutations.

Replay the saved draft on development data to verify correct routing, security precedence, SLA performance, backlog reduction, operator labor, and suppression of duplicate effects before requesting approval.

Request approval for the replayed draft: it achieved zero wrong routes and duplicate effects across all phases, preserved security precedence, and eliminated operator labor and backlog on the active development set. Stress and format-shift phases retained routing correctness; their remaining latency/backlog reflects queue capacity and unmatched-format manual fallback rather than unsafe misrouting, so the conservative draft is ready for authorization.

Deploy the exact approved configuration; its policy hash matches the replayed draft, which eliminated wrong routes and duplicate effects while preserving conservative manual fallback for unmatched formats.

Deployment succeeded with the exact approved policy hash 0b54490d11d71dcd7410ce346e616b40b6e9606b0ca35b96495303dce09040a5. Handoff: ticket-level deduplication is enabled; security-containment rules precede billing and access rules; unknown formats fall back to manual. Development replay showed zero wrong routes and duplicate effects across all phases, with the active set completing all 40 unique tickets on time and no backlog or operator labor. Capacity-limited stress and format-shift phases retained routing correctness but showed residual latency and, for format shift, 12 backlog events and 80 operator minutes; monitor those indicators for future rule coverage or capacity tuning.

source:
You operate an existing B2B customer support workflow. Investigate the supplied evidence,
infer the operational problem, and improve the executable routing configuration while
respecting the approval process. This is an authored simulation, not a real customer.

For mode=act, return one JSON Action matching the provided schema. Your observations and
history are the only task evidence. Start with inspect when useful. configure saves a
draft Policy; replay tests the draft on development data. request_approval authorizes
that exact configuration; deploy requires the approval_id from that response. Any new
configuration invalidates old approvals. finish ends your access and supplies a handoff
note. Configure rules with fields subject/body, substring contains, queue
manual/billing/access/security; rules use first-match case-insensitive evaluation.
fallback is one queue; deduplicate is a boolean. An empty rule list is allowed.

The objective is correct and timely processing with low operator labor and no duplicate
effects. Diagnose using evidence; do not invent measurements or read evaluator files.
Your reply is exactly one action JSON. The harness executes the action and returns the
next observation. Never claim that a draft has been deployed before deployment succeeds.

For mode=improve, return an Improvement JSON containing revised complete agent instructions
in source, and rationale. Use the supplied candidate instructions and development feedback
to improve its FDE workflow. You are changing the agent, not the evaluator or test data.
Preserve the action protocol and the ability of the next generation to perform improvement.
You have no final evaluation feedback. Do not report AGI or recursive improvement success.
